prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
(empty)

New part:
S001: This concept defines the operational scope and principal interfaces for operating and maintaining the offshore wind farm.
S002: The operational boundary covers the wind farm assets, offshore support facilities, control functions, and maintenance activities required to deliver safe electrical generation.
S003: The physical boundary begins at the turbine structures and includes the array of turbines and the Offshore Substation.
S004: The electrical boundary extends through the farm’s export connection to the point where the Grid Interface Relay represents the interface with the external grid.
S005: The concept includes the Turbine Controller, Pitch System, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Rotor Brake Unit, and Turbine Sensor Bus as representative turbine systems.
S006: It also includes the Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor, SCADA Gateway, and associated monitoring and control functions.
S007: The boundary ends at defined connections to shore-based control, grid operations, ports, suppliers, and emergency services.
S008: Public grid assets beyond the agreed connection point and port operations outside farm-related logistics are outside this concept.
S009: The primary operational objective is to generate electricity reliably while maintaining personnel safety and asset integrity.
S010: Availability objectives are pursued through condition monitoring, timely fault response, planned maintenance, and coordinated access to offshore assets.
S011: Safety objectives require work to be authorized, hazards to be controlled, and personnel and vessels to be accounted for throughout each operation.
S012: Environmental objectives include preventing pollution, minimizing disturbance to the marine environment, and responding promptly to environmental incidents.
S013: The operating model assigns continuous monitoring and dispatch coordination to the Shore Control Room.
S014: The lifecycle assumption is that the concept applies from commissioning and acceptance through routine operation, major refurbishment, and eventual decommissioning.
S015: During commissioning, the system is assumed to transition from construction control to operations control through documented handover and verification.
S016: During normal service, operating decisions are based on validated asset status, approved procedures, current forecasts, and applicable grid instructions.
S017: Planned maintenance is assumed to be scheduled around equipment condition, resource availability, access constraints, and production requirements.
S018: Unplanned maintenance is assumed to use prioritized fault assessment and controlled mobilization appropriate to the severity of the failure.
S019: At end of life, the concept supports safe isolation, removal planning, and transfer of residual operational records to the responsible organization.
S020: The control interface includes operational coordination with the Fleet Dispatch Console and Maintenance Planning Engine.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response: {"summary":"Offshore wind farm operations & maintenance concept. Scope: wind farm assets, offshore support facilities, control functions, maintenance for safe electrical generation. Physical boundary: turbine structures, turbine array, Offshore Substation. Electrical boundary: export connection up to Grid Interface Relay (interface to external grid). Turbine systems: Turbine Controller, Pitch System, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Rotor Brake Unit, Turbine Sensor Bus. Also: Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor, SCADA Gateway, monitoring/control functions. External interfaces: shore-based control, grid operations, ports, suppliers, emergency services. Out of scope: public grid assets beyond connection point; non-farm port operations. Shore Control Room: continuous monitoring and dispatch coordination. Control interface coordinates with Fleet Dispatch Console and Maintenance Planning Engine. Objectives: reliable generation with personnel safety and asset integrity; availability via condition monitoring, timely fault response, planned maintenance, coordinated access. Requirements: work shall be authorized, hazards controlled, personnel and vessels accounted for throughout operations; prevent pollution, minimize marine disturbance, respond promptly to environmental incidents. Lifecycle phases/modes: commissioning/acceptance (handover from construction control to operations control via documented handover and verification); normal service (decisions based on validated asset status, approved procedures, current forecasts, grid instructions); planned maintenance (scheduled by equipment condition, resources, access constraints, production needs); unplanned maintenance (prioritized fault assessment, controlled mobilization by severity); major refurbishment; decommissioning (safe isolation, removal planning, transfer of residual operational records to responsible organization)."}
